attempts.summary: On node1, created the datauser account and a dedicated 1 GiB loopback XFS filesystem mounted at /srv/data (via /etc/fstab, persistent), owned by datauser, with an XFS user quota of 100MB (bsoft=bhard=100m) set for datauser. Enforcement was verified by the kernel itself: a 150MB write as datauser was truncated to exactly 100M with "Disk quota exceeded", while a 10MB write succeeded. Performed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id/mount/quota/data, issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until exec was available again, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified the mount, quota configuration, existing data, and quota enforcement (repeat 150MB write again failed at 100MB) all survived and function correctly post-reboot.
